the investigation of self-organizing principles for the recognition of complex actions from RGB-D videos.
the study of self-organization in the brain and its application to visual recognition tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel self-organizing model for the recognition of transitive human actions from RGB-D data, which is able to learn action-object relationships in an unsupervized way.
the presented architecture is a self-organising system for learning action-object mappings from RGB-D video data.
the proposed model learns to recognize transitive actions by exploiting the co-occurrence of body motion and object identity in the input data, without the need of explicit supervision.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the self-organizing properties of GWR networks can be exploited to learn human-object interactions in a completely unsupervised fashion, without requiring the use of any external information or supervision.
the self-organizing properties of our neural network can be exploited for learning action-object mappings in a completely unsupervised fashion.

the proposed model can be trained in a self-supervised manner to learn action-object mappings, thus providing a novel and effective approach to address the problem of transitive human-object interactions recognition.
